name: Registration threshold

subjectOf.text: Under the Private Fund Investment Advisers Registration Act, hedge funds with more than $150 million in assets under management must register as investment advisers and disclose information about their trades and portfolios to the SEC, making assets under management the operative trigger for the regime.
subjectOf.abstract: Under the PFIARA, hedge funds with more than $150 million assets under management (AUM) are required to register as investment advisers and have to disclose information about their trades and portfolios to the SEC.81
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Fund Manager Registration Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2150377
scope_conditions: advisers acting solely as advisers to private funds
assets under management measured in the United States

subjectOf.text: Revised Form ADV requires advisers to report gross rather than net regulatory assets under management and narrows their discretion to include or exclude assets, so the registration threshold becomes harder to manage down through reporting choices.
subjectOf.abstract: To increase consistency, revised Form ADV also gives investment advisers less room to exercise discretion in counting or excluding assets from RAUM.115
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Fund Manager Registration Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2150377
scope_conditions: advisers filing the November 2011 revised Form ADV

subjectOf.text: The Title IV threshold registration requirement pulls a majority of the hedge fund advisers who had previously relied on the fewer than fifteen clients exemption into SEC registration.
subjectOf.abstract: The threshold registration requirement for private fund advisers under Title IV of the Dodd-Frank Act requires a majority of hedge fund advisers who had previously relied on the fewer than fifteen clients exemption31 to register with the SEC.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Investment Adviser Regulation (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2337268
scope_conditions: private fund advisers managing more than $150 million AUM

subjectOf.text: The clear majority of respondents prefer an asset size above the $150 million AUM registration threshold after the enactment of Title IV, indicating that advisers respond to the threshold by growing past it rather than staying below it.
subjectOf.abstract: The clear majority of respondents prefer an assets size above the registration threshold of $150 million AUM.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Impact of Dodd-Frank Act Compliance Cost on the Hedge Fund Industry (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389423
scope_conditions: survey responses on preferred asset size after Title IV enactment

subjectOf.abstract: Under PFIARA, hedge funds with more than $150 million AUM must register as investment advisers and disclose information about their trades and portfolios to the SEC.

subjectOf.text: Title IV requires private fund advisers with more than $150 million in assets under management to register with the SEC as investment advisers.
subjectOf.abstract: Title IV requires private fund advisers with more than $150 million assets under management (AUM) to register with the SEC as investment advisers.

subjectOf.text: Title IV exempts private fund advisers with less than $150 million assets under management from registration, and requires the SEC to weigh investment strategy, size, and governance in determining the systemic risk of private funds.
subjectOf.abstract: Title IV of the Dodd-Frank Act exempts private fund advisers with less than $150 million AUM from registration (Dodd-Frank Act § 408) and requires the SEC to examine factors including the investment strategy, size, and governance of an investment adviser
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Private Fund Performance  – Evidence from 2010 – 2015 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2816408
